# Twist fixture: naca2412_twist_c60_s60_w6.stl

## Description
A washed-out NACA 2412 wing: constant 60 mm chord, but the section rotates about the quarter-chord point by 6 degrees of washout from root (Z=0) to tip (Z=60 mm), linear in Z. Rotation axis: the quarter-chord point (25% of chord back from the leading edge, on the chord line), which stays at a fixed local X here because chord is constant, so it traces a straight line down the span. The rotation applied is +washout_deg (standard CCW-positive), which -- because the leading edge sits behind the pivot and the trailing edge sits ahead of it -- moves the leading edge toward -Y and the trailing edge toward +Y, i.e. the chord line tilts nose-down toward the tip: genuine washout (reduced incidence toward the tip), not washin -- confirmed below by the built geometry's own chord-line angle at root vs. tip.

## Origin convention
Same root-bounding-box-centring convention as the taper and sweep fixtures. Z is spanwise, root at Z=0, tip at Z=60 mm.

## Why many stations (not 2)
Rotation through an angle is not affine in Z: linearly interpolating between a 0-degree and a 6-degree-rotated outline does not equal the outline rotated by the interpolated angle at the midpoint (it cuts the chord of the rotation arc, not the arc itself). This fixture uses 61 stations (1 mm apart) so intermediate slices are genuinely rotated NACA sections, not a linear approximation of one.

## Purpose
M5 fixture: the cross-section rotates with Z. Exercises whether the structural pattern definition (web placement, intersection logic) stays sensible as the section's own orientation evolves down the span, independent of any chord change.

Generated by `python tools/make_fixtures.py twist --naca 2412 --chord 60 --span 60 --washout 6 --points 120 --stations 61`.
